correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact 32 distinct vertices in the quadratic ring Z[φ], φ²=φ+1, with 12 icosahedral and 20 dodecahedral orbit points. An independent enumeration compared both signed determinants and absolute determinant maxima for all C(32,4)=35,960 vertex quadruples using exact integer pair arithmetic, recovering exactly 20 maxima |det|=6+8φ and the 3-icosahedral/1-dodecahedral equilateral-apex description, with no two maximizing 4-sets sharing 3 vertices. Multiaffinity of signed volume on convex combinations gives a vertex optimum, and strict no-three-vertex-sharing forbids any nonvertex equality case. Dividing max determinant by six yields (5+2√5)/3. Face pyramids give body volume 20 and sharp ratio (5+2√5)/60; the known 10 dodecahedral compound tetrahedra have smaller 8/3 volume.

evidence: One comparable result is for the 12-vertex icosahedron only; its feasible tetrahedra are a strict subset of those in 32-vertex triacontahedron and do not control additional dodecahedral vertices. Other family is an octahedron–cube intersection, not this zonohedron.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader-sounding simplex optimization does not dominate the present containing body; exact vertex-addition case is unaddressed.
